# What differs between two runs of scripts/datafix-worlds.sh for the same version, as `worldcmp --ignore-field` specs
# (one per line, syntax in tools/worldcmp/src/fields.rs). With these left out, the scripted (flat) worlds of 1.7.10,
# 1.12.2, 1.13.2, 1.16.5, 1.20.4, 1.21.5 and 26.2 generated twice compare clean:
#
#   args=(); while read -r s; do args+=(--ignore-field "$s"); done < <(grep -vE '^(#|$)' world_run_dependent.txt)
#   worldcmp WORLD_A WORLD_B --tree "${args[@]}"
#
# Why each group differs:
#  - session.lock, LastPlayed, Time, LastUpdate, ticks of the saved data: wall clock and the number of ticks the server ran.
#  - rain/thunder timers: drawn from the clock-seeded random of a new server.
#  - game_rules.dat of 26.x: the rules are stored in hash order, which differs between runs.
#  - furnace, brewing stand, beehive and sculk sensor counters: tick-driven, and the number of ticks differs.
#  - Entities: random UUIDs, rotations and movement, chickens laying eggs, so no entity list is comparable (the entity
#    files of 1.17+ and Level.Entities of older releases are left out as a whole).
#  - The other dimensions: they are generated at the server's pace, so which chunks exist and how far each got differs.
#  - Section block data, heightmaps, Status: chunks at the edge of the loaded area depend on the generation order of their
#    neighbours. The scripted blocks stay covered through block entities and the unchanged parts of every other file.
# The seed-12345 worlds (<id>-normal) are not reproducible bit for bit at all: the set of generated chunks and their
# generation stage depends on how fast the server ran during the 60 s wait. Their world_hashes only identify the copy
# in the cache.
